project.name: Arnis
project.description: Generate real life cities in Minecraft. Creates complex and accurate Minecraft Java Edition, Bedrock Edition and Luanti worlds that reflect real-world geography, topography, and architecture.

tags.description: Used to generate buildings, with the value choosing the style, typical height, roof and interior.
Generates each part as its own volume with its own height, min_height and roof, styled like the rest of its building.
Groups a building outline with its building:part members, which share one style. The outline is left out when the parts cover at least half of it.
Used to set a building's height from its number of storeys, more than seven storeys giving it a tall building style.
Used to determine the starting elevation level for elevated buildings.
Used to lift a building or building part off the ground by this many metres, its walls running from there up to height.
Used to set the height of buildings and building parts, roof included, and of towers, masts, trees, barriers and other structures.
Used to determine the color of building walls and materials.

Used to date a building, so that its era picks the wall palette, window style and ornament.
Used like start_date when that tag is missing.
Marks a building as listed, giving it an ornate historic facade with more detail unless it is dated after 1945.

Lifts roads with a positive layer onto decks and sets the height of bridge decks and roof canopies, while layer -2 and below sinks road tunnels deeper. Buildings and most small features with a negative layer are not generated.

Used to paint the ground and scatter plants, trees and props on land use areas such as farmland, forests, meadows, cemeteries, quarries and construction sites. Residential and commercial areas are skipped.

Used to generate natural features including trees, water bodies, wetlands, beaches, and terrain features. Names of landforms such as peninsulas, valleys and mountain ranges are ignored, since they take in towns and fields alike.
Places a tree whose kind follows its genus, species, taxon or leaf_type tag and whose size follows height.

Generates woodland areas with trees and forest vegetation.

Generates sand, with occasional dead bushes in desert and steppe climates.
Generates sand dune terrain.
Generates a sand beach, or gravel, stone or mud when surface says so.

Generates reef areas with water blocks.

Generates ridge areas (elevated crests) with predominantly rocky terrain.
Generates tundra terrain with low vegetation and moss.
Generates hilly terrain with grass and sparse trees.
Generates cliff areas with predominantly stone terrain.
Raises the terrain to the summit height given in ele where the elevation data falls short.
Used on natural=peak and volcano nodes to lift the terrain to the surveyed summit height in metres.
Places a cross on a small cobblestone cairn at a peak, volcano or hill node.
Used to choose broadleaf or conifer trees for forests, woods, tree rows and single trees.
Limits trees to broadleaf kinds such as oak and birch.
Limits trees to spruce and pine.
Picks the tree model of that genus for single trees and tree rows, such as birch for Betula.
Used like genus, from its first word, when genus is missing.
Used like genus, from its first word, when genus and species are missing.
Used to specify the type of wetland for appropriate vegetation generation.

Generates fen areas without standing water.
Generates reedbed areas with tall grass vegetation.
Generates swamp areas with trees and water.

Generates tidal flat areas without vegetation.

Used to cut water channels along rivers, streams, canals and ditches, sized by waterway type or width, and to fill docks and riverbank areas with water. Waterways in tunnels are skipped.
